sections.html:
Three moves are on the table for a Jackson owner who needs to sell soon: a regular listing, a private deal with a buyer you already know, or a cash purchase of the house as it stands. The decision tends to follow the calendar and the state of the roof, plumbing and foundation.

As county seat and West Tennessee's trade center, Jackson can draw listing buyers from surrounding counties. Yet a house with postponed repairs may go through many showings while inspectors note every flaw. A cash buyer accounts for those flaws once, in the price, and closes when you say.

  • Listing: the broadest audience, but repair requests follow each inspection.
  • Private sale: cheaper marketing and more paperwork for you.
  • Cash purchase: a single decision on a house sold as is.

Jackson goes by the Hub City, and it covers 58.44 square miles of land, 70 miles from Memphis to the west and 130 miles from Nashville to the northeast. Six exits serve Interstate 40 as it passes through. Highland Avenue is the local name for U.S. 45, the north-south route, and the Keith Short bypass on the west side diverts truck traffic. Air service flies from McKellar-Sipes Regional Airport, and Jackson Transit Authority buses cover the city.

A trip to work averages 18.2 minutes, a point to share with any buyer employed in town. Children attend the consolidated Jackson-Madison County School System.

Jackson had an estimated 69,339 residents on July 1, 2025, which is 1.7 percent over the 2020 base. Housing divides nearly evenly between owners and renters.

  • Homes lived in by owners: 51.2 percent
  • Typical value of an owner's home: $217,800
  • Middle gross rent: $1,145
  • Middle household income: $53,032
  • Households: 27,541, averaging 2.34 people

Since so many households rent, a seller with a rental or an older house should be ready for buyer questions on tenants, rents and repair costs.

sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill
sections.html:
Inside city limits a house is billed twice, by two offices. The City Revenue Office issues the city bill, and the Madison County Trustee issues the county bill. Values for both come from the county Assessor of Property, which does not bill or accept payment.

Offices behind a Jackson property tax bill
OfficeRolePhone
Assessor of Property, courthouse third floorValues, reviews, address updates731-423-6063
Madison County TrusteeCounty tax billing and payment731-423-6027
City of Jackson Revenue OfficeCity tax billing and payment731-425-8210

Notices land around the first week of October, and early payment is not possible. A tax figure on a closing statement dated before October 1 is only an estimate. The roll keeps the January 1 owner's name all year, so have your closing attorney walk you through how the bill is shared.

The next countywide reappraisal is 2027, after 2022. Median home sale price reached $251,450 in January 2026 against $212,500 four years before, a climb of about 18.33 percent, so higher notices are likely.

Your first call goes to the assessor, who can verify that the record fits the house. Still unhappy? Five local owners sit on the county Board of Equalization, which hears appeals on weekdays in the first two weeks of June; appointments open in late May. Madison County warns that an earlier year's taxes cannot be appealed afterward.

The State Board of Equalization is the next level up. Its deadline is August 1, or 45 days after the county's written decision if that is later. Helpful evidence: sales of similar houses nearby, a paid appraisal, and photos inside and out.

sections.h2: Recording at the Madison County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Recording happens at the courthouse, 100 East Main Street, Suite 109 (731-423-6028), weekdays nine to five. The office holds land records back to 1821 and offers property alert sign-up. Instructions say a deed gets stamped first, then goes to the Register.

The state transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price. Removing a deceased co-owner from tax records takes a death certificate when the person is on the deed. When not, a probated will is required. Phone 731-423-6063 about that step.

sections.h2: Permits inside and outside the city
sections.html:
Houses inside city limits involve two calls: the city's Building and Codes Department at 731-425-8262 and the Madison County Building Department at 731-423-6014. Outside the city, call only the county.

Madison County wants permits pulled for remodels, room additions, storm or flood repairs and new construction so its property records stay accurate. Collect the permit papers for recent work before you list. City business licenses come from the Revenue Office in the west end of City Hall, which is open from 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays.

sections.h2: Other costs and chores for a Jackson seller
sections.html:
• Get the balance on each bill from the City Revenue Office and from the County Trustee.
  • Give the assessor a forwarding address, so the next notice reaches you.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter good through the closing date.
  • An appeal to the State Board carries a filing fee of $10 to $17, and part of it cannot be refunded.

Recorded loans, including a buyer's, also owe a state mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 once the first $2,000 is exempt. Before comparing offers, have each one spell out who pays title and recording charges, so the net proceeds line up. Cash offers shorten the chores, since no appraisal or buyer's lender stands in the way.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or inherited house in Jackson
sections.html:
Rentals and inherited houses bring extra homework in Jackson. For a rental, collect copies of each lease, the current rent amounts and receipts for repairs, because buyers will ask. A buyer who pays cash can often take a house with tenants in it, and any plan for the tenant can be written into the contract.

For an inherited house, work out who is authorized to sign. When someone on the deed has died, the assessor's office can remove the name once it receives a death certificate. When the person was not on the deed, a probated will is required. Sort this out before listing, since a title company will not close until the ownership question is settled.

Pick your route first, then take these in order. Find the two tax balances. Order a lender payoff letter. Gather permit papers for recent work. Once an offer is accepted, the closing attorney or title company confirms ownership, divides the tax bill by the January 1 rule and files the deed at the courthouse. A mortgage buyer adds an appraisal and loan approval to that list, while a cash buyer does not.

faqs.q: Does a Jackson homeowner pay two property tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes when the house is within city limits. The City Revenue Office bills one and the Madison County Trustee bills the other. Beyond the city line, only the county bill applies.

faqs.q: What year is Madison County's next reappraisal?
faqs.a: The next round is in 2027, after the one in 2022. Value appeals each year go to the county Board of Equalization in June.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Jackson sale?
faqs.a: State law sets it at $0.37 for every $100 of price. Your contract decides who pays.

faqs.q: Where does a Jackson deed get recorded?
faqs.a: The Madison County Register of Deeds takes it, in Suite 109 of the courthouse at 100 East Main Street, Jackson, TN 38301. Call 731-423-6028; weekday hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: How do I take a deceased owner's name off a Jackson property record?
faqs.a: Phone the Madison County Assessor, 731-423-6063. If the deceased owner is on the deed, a death certificate does it. If not, a probated will is required.
